Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Class P2pNode

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.P2pNode
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable, SecureChannel.Listener
public final class P2pNode extends Object implements SecureChannel.Listener, AutoCloseable
One participant in the encrypted peer-to-peer mesh: a long-term identity, an inbound P2pServer, outbound dialling, and a peer map. A node owns every SecureChannel it establishes and routes each channel's frames to a per-peer FileTransferManager and to the node P2pNode.Listener, so the two apps (Messenger, Video Conference) see peers, chat, presence, invites and file transfers rather than sockets.

Identity. Each node holds a static X25519 KeyPair; the SHA-256 fingerprint of its public key is the node's identity and the key by which peers are tracked. The caller supplies the keypair so persistence stays outside this class (the app store's IdentityStore owns it at rest).

Trust. A P2pNode.PeerVerifier hook is consulted with a peer's fingerprint right after the handshake and before it joins the mesh; the default verifier accepts everyone, and the TOFU pinning layer installs a real one. An untrusted peer is closed immediately and never added to the map.

Threading. The constructor is inert (headless-safe: it opens no socket and starts no thread). start(int) binds the server; connect(java.lang.String, int) dials out. Listener callbacks fire on channel reader threads, the server accept threads or file-transfer workers - never the Swing EDT - so callers marshal to the EDT before touching any widget. All threads are daemons.

The mesh suits 1:1 and small groups, not large-scale networks; that honest boundary is documented for the UI. Reachability is direct connections plus LAN auto-discovery (see LanDiscovery); internet peers need port-forwarding or a reachable host - there is no NAT hole-punching here.

  • Field Details

    • PROLOGUE

      public static final byte[] PROLOGUE
      The shared handshake prologue. Binding every channel to this context stops a channel established for one purpose being replayed into another, and both sides must agree on it (they do - it is a constant of the transport).

    • STATUS_ONLINE

  • Constructor Details

    • P2pNode

      public P2pNode(KeyPair identity, String nickname, Path downloadDir, P2pNode.Listener listener)
      Creates an inert node. No socket is opened and no thread is started until start(int) or connect(java.lang.String, int).
      Parameters:
      identity - the node's long-term static keypair (never null)
      nickname - our display name (blank falls back to a fingerprint tag)
      downloadDir - where received files are written (null falls back to a lg3d-p2p dir under the temporary directory)
      listener - the event sink (may be null)
